key_insight: You can make reasoning models stop earlier without directly training them to be short. Self-supervised confidence signals are enough to improve reasoning efficiency while preserving strong reasoning performance.
problem_solved: Reasoning models often produce unnecessarily long chains of thought, increasing latency and compute cost. This paper addresses how to reduce inference-time reasoning length without relying on explicit early-stopping rules or length-penalized training.
method: Train the model with self-supervised confidence supervision, using confidence as the signal for when reasoning is sufficient.
Avoid explicit length penalties or direct 'learn to stop' objectives; instead, teach the model to estimate when it already knows the answer.
Use the confidence-trained model to terminate reasoning earlier, improving efficiency while maintaining accuracy.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a simpler path to faster and cheaper reasoning systems. It can lower token usage and latency without requiring manual stopping heuristics or heavily modifying the reasoning objective.

paper_title: Learning to Stop without Learning to Stop: Self-Supervised Confidence Training Improves Reasoning Efficiency
paper_authors: Parsa Hosseini, Akasha Tigalappanavara, Sumit Nawathe, Chenrui Fan, Sourya Basu
